Judgment

1. Vide this judgment, I propose to dispose of the appeal filed by the appellants challenging the order dated 07.08.2019 whereby the Ld. Adjudicating Officer inter alia held the appellants guilty for violating the provisions under Sections 23, 26(1), 26(2)(ii) & 27 (30(c) read with Section 3(1)(zf)(a)(i) of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 ("FSS Act" in short) and Regulation No.
2.2.1.3 read with 2.3.1.5 of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labeling) Regulations,
2011 (in short "FSS (P&L) Regulation"), punishable under Section 52 of the FSS Act and imposed a penalty of Rs.50,000/ on the appellants.
2.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labeling) Regulations
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
In brief, the facts are that Sh. Hukum Singh, FSO, purchased a sample of 'basmati rice' from Sh.
Sumit Bansal, FBOcumnominee of M/s AB Hotel Ltd. (Redission Blu Hotel), NH8, Mahipalpur,
New Delhi, on 07.06.2017.

entities.text: AB Hotel Ltd. (Redission Blu Hotel), NH8,
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Food Analyst vide his report bearing No. FSS/654/2017 dated 20.06.2017 held that the sample is misbranded because there is violation of Regulation no. 2.2.1.3 and 2.3.1.5 of FSS (P&L) Regulations.
The application under Rule 3.1.1(3) of FSS Rules, 2011, was filed before the Ld. Adjudicating Officer for prosecution of Sh. Sumit Bansal, FBOcumnominee of M/s AB Hotel Ltd (Redission Blu Hotel).

The application was also filed against Mrs. Madhu Manchanda, Proprietor of M/s P.K. Trading Co. and Sh. Vinod Kumar Manchanda, Proprietory of Mrs. Madhu Manchanda vs Department Of Food Safety on 21 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53008448/
1 M/s Trimax International.

The prosecution was sought on the following grounds :
"1. Label declaration "GMO free" is misleading and likely to create an erroneous impression regarding its character.
2. Expiry date given in place of Best before Declaration."
3. Ld.

Adjudicating Officer after hearing the submissions of the parties inter alia, held that the label of the sample was in violation of provisions of FSS Act and thus, held the respondents guilty for violation of the provisions of FSS Act, 2006 and FSS (P&L) Regulations, 2011.

Respondent no. 3&4 (appellants herein) invoked the jurisdiction of this court and filed the present appeal under the provision of FSS Act, challenging the impugned order on the ground that the order passed by the Ld.
Adjudicating Officer is erroneous, both on facts as well as on law.

The appellants submitted that the copy of the Food Analyst Report was not given to them and therefore, they did not get the opportunity to challenge the same and the same is in violation of Rule 3.1.1(1)(2) and (3) of FSS Rules, 2011.

It has further been submitted that as per the report issued by the Food Analyst, the sample of rice contained therein retains all its qualities, however, the 'date of expiry' and declaration of 'GMO free' was held to be in violation of Rule 2.2.1.3 & 2.3.1.5 FSS (P&L) Regulations, 2011.
It has further been submitted that as per the report of Food Analyst, the rice sold by the appellant was in fact 'GMO free' and there was no false or misleading declaration on the packaging.
It has been submitted that the appellants are wholesale suppliers of rice to hotels and caterers, who require the product in large quantities to be cooked and sold in events, hotels guests, etc.
It has been further submitted that the goods are not available in super market/small store/general store for sale to the consumers directly.

It has been submitted that declaration made by the appellants on the packaging was done with the purpose to increase the consumer awareness and at the best, it is an additional declaration, which is not false or misleading.
It has been submitted that in the markets of European Unions, such kind of declaration is essential.
It has been submitted that date of "best before", "date of last consumption" and "date of expiry" are used synonymously in the FSS Act per se and therefore, the conclusion of the Ld.
Adjudicating Officer
that the appellants have violated Regulation 2.2.1.3 read with 2.3.1.5, is arbitrary and unlawful.
4. The notice of the appeal was issued to the respondent and the TCR was called.
5. Ms. Aarti Manchanda, Ld. Counsel for the appellants has submitted that the subject matter of the present appeal is packaging in question and not the quality of product.
It has been submitted that the appellants are supplier of rice to hotels and caterers.

They received one such order from Radisson Blu and they supplied the goods as per the specifications in packaging with clear declaration on the back side of the bag "25kg Special Pack for Whole Sale".
It has been further submitted that the orders are received by the appellants on a weekly basis, thus, question of expiry of the product does not arise.
Ld. Counsel further submitted that the appellants filed packaging of other rice manufacturers, who sold their goods in the super markets, ration shops etc. and contained the same declaration.
Ld. Counsel further submitted that even as per Food Analyst report, the product was not genetically modified and therefore, the declaration was not false under any provisions of FSS Act.

The declaration was made with the purpose to increase the consumer Mrs. Madhu Manchanda vs Department Of Food Safety on 21 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53008448/
2 awareness.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It has been further submitted that the provisions of FSS (P&L) Regulations, 2011, are applicable on goods available for sale in pre packaged form and not in the cooked form and since,
the product was sold with a clear declaration of "Special Pack for Whole Sale", the above provisions do not apply on the appellants.

It has been further submitted that the appellants have not made any false claim on its packaging and neither misled the consumer and the appellants have rather kept in mind the Indian as well as International standards in ensuring the quality of food sold to Radisson Blu.

6. Sh. Kundan Kohli, Ld. Chief PP for the State has submitted that the label declaration "GMO free"
is misleading and likely to create an erroneous impression regarding its character.
It has been submitted that 'expiry date' is given in place of 'Best Before Declaration', which is in violation of Regulation 2.2.1.3 read with 2.3.1.5 of FSS (P&L) Regulation, 2011.
It has been further submitted that when the legislature has provided the format/manner, the appellants were required to follow it strictly.
It has been submitted that a label should not contain any abbreviation, which is misleading in any particular, concerning the food contained in the package or concerning the quality of the said food.
7. I have heard the submissions of both the parties and perused the record carefully.

8. The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, was enacted to avoid any confusion in the mind of consumers, traders, manufacturers and investors in view of multiplicity of food laws, standards setting and enforcement agencies relating to different sectors of food.
It was thought there should be one comprehensive legislation on Food with a Food Regulatory Authority concerning both domestic and export markets.
The main objective of the Act is to bring out a single statute relating to food and to provide for a systematic and scientific development of Food Processing Industries.

The main object was to fix food standards and regulate/monitor the manufacturing, import, processing,
distribution and sale of food, so as to ensure safe and wholesome food for the people.
In order to achieve the above objectives, besides Act, the rules were also framed to cover all attendant factors.

In the present case, predominantly the prosecution was launched against the appellants Mrs. Madhu Manchanda and Sh. V.K. Manchanda, as it was found that there was misbranding on account of the fact that the appellants in their brand have given 'expiry date' in place of 'best before' declaration and that appellants have written "GMO free" whereas, there was no requirement of the same.
9. It is an admitted case that the sample was found 'not genetic modified'.
The plea of the Ld. Chief PP for the State is that by writing "GMO free", appellants have created a confusion in the minds of consumers.
10. Per contra, the plea of the respondents (appellants herein) is that in fact they have been extra careful in writing "GMO free", as it is a requirement at present under international law.
Ld. Counsel has submitted that since the sample was not found genetically modified, there is no question of any intention of cheating or creating confusion in the minds of consumers.
11. I consider that since the sample commodity was not found genetically modified, the appellants cannot be held liable for the misbranding.
It is a matter of record that Report of the Food Analyst Mrs. Madhu Manchanda vs Department Of Food Safety on 21 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53008448/

entities.text: Report of the Food Analyst Mrs. Madhu Manchanda vs Department Of Food Safety on 21 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3 does not say that the sample was found genetic modified or there was any deficiency in the food quality of the sample.
There is force in the submission of the appellants that the appellants have merely been overcautious in view of the best practices adopted at international level.
I do not consider that there is any ground even to consider that it may create confusion in the mind of general public.

12. In respect of other plea of 'best before' declaration, it is advantageous to refer to Regulation No.2.2.2.10 of FSS (P&L) Regulations, 2011, which stipulates the month and year in capital letters up to which the product is best for consumption.

The Act provides that the same has to be provided in the following manner:
"BEST BEFORE ....... MONTHS AND YEAR OR "BEST BEFORE .......... MONTHS FROM PACKAGING OR "BEST BEFORE ............MONTHS FROM MANUFACTURE"
13.
From the plain reading of the above provision, it is evident that the declaration on the label did not strictly conform to Regulation 2.2.2.10 of FSS (P&L) Regulations.

As per the Section 3(1)(zf)(C)(i) of the FSA Act, an article of food shall be rendered misbranded if the package containing such article is not labeled in accordance with the requirements of the Act or regulations made thereunder.
14. It is an admitted case that on the sample of rice bag, the word 'date of expiry' is written in place of 'best before'.

The plea of the appellants is that the declaration as required by the Act has been given in the label in most unambiguous manner and therefore, there is sufficient compliance of Regulation No.2.2.2.10 of FSS (P&L) Regulations.
15.

Considering that the sample food article did mention the expiry date and the consumer had a reference date, as packaging is either subsequent to or simultaneous with the manufacturing, the consumer did have a reference date to know the date up to which the sample food article was best consumed.

It may be mentioned that in somewhat similar situation, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi vide its judgment dated 06.02.2009 in Crl. M.C. No. 3307/2007 titled S.S. Gokul Krishnan Ors Vs.
State, held that the sample food article cannot be said to be misbranded and noted as under :
"19.

entities.text:
S.S. Gokul Krishnan Ors Vs.
State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, declaration under rule 32(i) is best before 9 months from packing.

Since the month and year of manufacture of the food article i.e. processed cheese is clearly disclosed on the packet, it cannot be said that the consumer would be misled from the terms best before 9 months from packing.
The consumer, under these circumstances, would be clear in his mind to consider the best before from the date of manufacturing....
20. Prima facie, therefore, it cannot be said that the sample was misbranded because misleading statement was given on the label with respect to best before date..."

16. It would be pertinent to refer here to the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Ram Babu Rastogi and others V. State, Through Food Inspector (PFA)2012(1) FAC 56, wherein in somewhat Mrs. Madhu Manchanda vs Department Of Food Safety on 21 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53008448/
4 similar situation, the Hon'ble High Court in para no. 14 observed as under :
"14.

entities.text: Ram Babu Rastogi and others V. State, Through Food Inspector (PFA)2012(1) FAC 56
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Mrs. Madhu Manchanda vs Department Of Food Safety on 21 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The actual label found at the sample article i.e. "Best before within 6 months from date of packaging"
conveyed much more than which was required to be conveyed to the purchasers about the genuineness of the product.
Mere use of word "within" as a surplusage would not bring the petitioners under the penal provisions of the Act.
By any means, the purchasers could not be said to have been deceived or misled as regards the character, quantity, quality or date of manufacture and the limit of use of the product."

17. In M.D. Anand Aqua, M/s S.B. Industries, Patna Vs. The State of Bihar & another, 2011(1) FAC 265, and Oscar Joseph & another Vs. The State of Jharkhand and another, 2012(2) FAC 74, the label did not mention the words BEST BEFORE in capital letters and rather, mentioned it in small letters.

entities.text: M.D. Anand Aqua, M/s S.B. Industries, Patna Vs. The State of Bihar & another, 2011(1) FAC 265
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Oscar Joseph & another Vs. The State of Jharkhand and another, 2012(2) FAC 74
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, the Hon'ble Patna High Court noted that there was a sufficient compliance.

In Pramod Kumar Kediya Vs The State of Bihar and another, 2012(1)FAC 479, similar view was taken by Hon'ble Patna High Court with respect to mentioning of date of manufacturing and expiry in small letters though required to be written in capital letters.

entities.text: Pramod Kumar Kediya Vs The State of Bihar and another, 2012(1)FAC 479
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18. In view of the above facts and circumstances and the position of law as discussed above, the label on the sample commodity can be said to have sufficiently complied with Regulation 2.2.2.10 FSS (P&L) Regulations.
The sample food article cannot be said to be misbranded.
The impugned order dated 07.08.2019 is set aside and the appeal is allowed.
19. TCR be sent back alongwith copy of the judgment.
20. File be consigned to Record Room.
